en.title: Largest Square from Small and Large Tiles
en.description:
There are m tiles of size 1×1 and n tiles of size 2×2. You may choose some of the tiles to form a square on a grid with no overlaps and no gaps. Find the maximum integer side length.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: One line m n, 0≤m,n≤10⁹. The original range gives a lower bound of 1, but the source's examples explicitly include 0, so this site also keeps the zero-tile cases.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: 8 unit tiles can only form side length 2, since they are not enough for 9 cells. Example 2: three large tiles plus four small tiles fill a 4×4 square. Example 3: using only large tiles, the largest even side length is 8, which uses 16 tiles and leaves 2.
hints: First take the square root L of the total area. An even side length is limited only by the total area; an odd L needs at least 2L−1 unit tiles, and if there are not enough, drop to L−1.
